title: Reason, Mysticism, and Skepticism
summary: Reason as the only means of knowledge, and mysticism and skepticism as denials of it.

lessons.title: The only means of knowledge
lessons.objective: Reason is the only means of knowledge and the only standard of truth.

exercises.prompt: On this unit’s view, what is the only means of knowledge?

choices.text: Reason
Faith
Whatever you feel at the moment
A show of hands

feedback.note: Knowledge is gained by reason. No other method is granted that job.

exercises.prompt: What is truth, in this lesson?

choices.text: The recognition of reality
Whatever you wish were so
A matter of literary style
A message hidden from the mind

feedback.note: A true claim recognizes what is. It does not invent a private version of the facts.

exercises.prompt: What is the only standard of truth?

choices.text: Reason
Local custom
How loudly a claim is made
How old a claim is

feedback.note: Because reason is the only means of knowledge, it is also the only standard for judging a claim true.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to its role.

feedback.note: Reason does the knowing. Truth is the recognition it reaches. Feelings do not take either job.

exercises.prompt: Complete the claim about how you know.

parts.text: Reason is the only means of

feedback.note: The blank is knowledge. Comfort, status, and mystery are not means of knowing the facts.

exercises.prompt: Build the lesson’s main claim.

feedback.note: Faith is not a second means, and reason is not optional if you want knowledge.

exercises.prompt: Complete the claim about judging truth.

parts.text: Reason is the only standard of

feedback.note: A claim is true when reason recognizes reality, not when it matches taste, loyalty, or speed.

exercises.prompt: Match each proposed shortcut to why it fails.

feedback.note: Shortcuts can feel decisive. They still do not identify the facts in reason’s place.

exercises.prompt: Two claims conflict. What settles which one recognizes reality?

choices.text: Reason applied to the facts
Whichever claim is older
Whichever speaker is louder
Whichever claim feels nicer

feedback.note: Age, volume, and comfort are not standards. Reason is the court that checks a claim against reality.

lessons.title: Mysticism
lessons.objective: Mysticism claims a way of knowing that bypasses reason, such as faith, revelation, or feeling used as proof.

exercises.prompt: What does mysticism claim?

choices.text: A means of knowledge other than reason
That reason is the only means of knowledge
That only arithmetic counts as thought
That the senses should be sharpened by practice

feedback.note: Mysticism does not refine reason. It offers a rival route to knowledge.

exercises.prompt: Match each mystical stand-in to what it is asked to do.

pairs.right: Treat a disclosed message as knowledge
Let a mood decide the facts

feedback.note: Faith, revelation, and feeling-as-proof skip the work of identifying reality by reason.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is mysticism, not ordinary reasoning?

choices.text: A private revelation is said to prove a fact reason cannot check
You recheck a measurement because the first reading looks off
You define a term before you argue with it
You ask what evidence supports a news claim

feedback.note: Checking, defining, and asking for evidence are uses of reason. A non-rational revelation is the rival.

exercises.prompt: Complete the description of mysticism.

feedback.note: The thing bypassed is reason. Hope, art, and memory are not the means mysticism is rejecting.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about mysticism’s claim.

feedback.note: Mysticism puts forward another means. It does not claim to be a stricter use of reason.

exercises.prompt: Someone says a warm feeling proves a historical fact. What is that move?

choices.text: Mysticism: feeling is used as a means of knowledge
Reason: the feeling integrated the evidence
Skepticism: the person denied that any fact can be known
A check: the person compared two records

feedback.note: A feeling can report your estimate. Offered as proof of a fact, it is a mystical substitute for reason.

exercises.prompt: Match each mystical claim to the denial it makes.

pairs.right: Denies that reason is the only means
Denies that knowledge must be reasoned

pairs.left: If it feels true, it is true
pairs.right: Denies reason as the standard of truth

feedback.note: Each form keeps the word knowledge but drops reason as the only way to get it.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line about faith.

parts.text: Faith is not a means of

feedback.note: Faith may name a commitment. It is not accepted here as a way of knowing reality.

exercises.prompt: Build what mysticism does to reason’s status.

feedback.note: The denial is specific: reason is not the only means. Mysticism still talks as if knowledge is available by another route.

lessons.title: Skepticism
lessons.objective: Skepticism denies that knowledge is possible, and so denies that reason succeeds.

exercises.prompt: What does skepticism claim about knowledge?

choices.text: Knowledge is not possible
Reason is the only means of knowledge
Faith supplies what reason misses
Every opinion is already knowledge

feedback.note: Skepticism does not offer a better method. It says the goal, knowledge, cannot be reached.

exercises.prompt: Which move is skepticism, not a use of reason?

choices.text: A blanket claim that no one can know reality
Retesting one result that conflicts with the others
Asking which evidence a conclusion rests on
Saying you do not know this fact yet

feedback.note: A particular doubt still uses reason. Skepticism denies knowledge as such.

exercises.prompt: Match each skeptical line to what it denies.

pairs.right: Denies any standard that could rank claims

feedback.note: These lines do not correct one error. They wipe out the possibility of a reasoned conclusion.

exercises.prompt: Complete the skeptical claim.

feedback.note: The target word is possible. Skepticism is about whether knowledge can be had, not about whether it is pleasant.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about what skepticism denies.

feedback.note: The denial lands on reason’s success. It is not a claim that faith invents a new world.

exercises.prompt: How is skepticism unlike mysticism?

choices.text: It says no means of knowledge succeeds
It adds revelation as a second means
It is just another name for reason
It treats a feeling as proof

feedback.note: Mysticism substitutes a means. Skepticism says you cannot know, so reason fails along with every rival.

exercises.prompt: Match each action to the right label.

pairs.left: I do not know this yet
pairs.right: A limit on one claim, not skepticism
Use of the means of knowledge

feedback.note: Not knowing one fact yet leaves reason in place. Declaring knowledge impossible does not.

exercises.prompt: Complete what skepticism says about reason.

feedback.note: If knowledge is impossible, reason does not work as a means of knowledge. That is the denial.

exercises.prompt: A skeptic says a careful proof and a guess are equally unsupported. What has been dropped?

choices.text: Reason as a standard that can rank claims
Faith as a required extra step
Only the wording of the proof
Only the names of the speakers

feedback.note: If no claim can be better supported than another, reason is no longer a standard of truth.

lessons.title: What rejecting reason licenses
lessons.objective: Rejecting reason means acting with no regard for the facts, or against them.

exercises.prompt: If reason is rejected, what guide to action is left?

choices.text: None that tracks the facts
A stricter means of knowledge
Knowledge that arrives with no method
The senses used with no identification at all, still called knowledge

feedback.note: Reason is the means of grasping reality. Drop it, and action is no longer guided by knowledge of the facts.

exercises.prompt: Match each result of rejecting reason.

pairs.left: Acting in contradiction to the facts

feedback.note: Without reason as the means of knowledge, action can bypass the facts or collide with them.

exercises.prompt: Complete one result of rejecting reason.

parts.text: People may act regardless of the

feedback.note: The loss is contact with the facts. Fashion, rumor, and title are not what reason was tracking.

exercises.prompt: Build the other result.

feedback.note: Rejecting reason does not prove a new truth. It leaves action free to contradict reality.

exercises.prompt: A person knows the bridge is out and crosses because a feeling says otherwise. What is that?

choices.text: Action in contradiction to the facts
Reason used as the standard of truth
A decision to learn one fact that is still unknown
Only a change of the bridge’s name

feedback.note: The feeling is allowed to overrule a known fact. That is action against reality, not a use of reason.

exercises.prompt: A crew never asks whether the dose is safe and ships it anyway. What is that pattern?

choices.text: Acting regardless of the facts
Integrating the evidence before acting
A proof that knowledge is impossible
A mere relabeling of the same careful test

feedback.note: They do not contradict a known result so much as refuse to look. Action proceeds with no regard for the facts.

exercises.prompt: Match each stance to the action it supports.

pairs.left: Reason kept as the means of knowledge
pairs.right: Act on what the facts support

pairs.left: A revelation in place of reason
pairs.right: Act on a claim reason did not establish

pairs.left: The claim that nothing can be known
pairs.right: No knowledge left to guide action

feedback.note: Only the first stance still ties action to knowledge. The other two have dropped that tie.

exercises.prompt: Complete the cost in one word for the thing abandoned.

parts.text: Rejecting reason abandons the only means of

feedback.note: What is abandoned is knowledge as a guide. The cost shows up when people act anyway.

exercises.prompt: Build why the rejection matters for action.

feedback.note: Knowledge was the guide. Reject the only means of knowledge, and action loses that guide.

lessons.title: Three answers about knowledge
lessons.objective: Sort reason, mysticism, and skepticism by what each says about whether and how you can know.

exercises.prompt: Match each stance to its claim.

feedback.note: Reason affirms one means. Mysticism adds or substitutes a means. Skepticism says the attempt fails.

exercises.prompt: Which stance affirms that you can know reality by reason?

choices.text: Reason as the only means of knowledge
Mysticism
Skepticism
Mysticism and skepticism together

feedback.note: Only the first stance keeps reason as a working means. The other two deny that status, in different ways.

exercises.prompt: A teacher says revelation knows truths reason must not judge. Which label fits?

choices.text: Mysticism
Skepticism
Reason as the only standard of truth
An admission that one fact is not known yet

feedback.note: The claim still offers knowledge, but by a route reason is forbidden to judge. That is mysticism.

exercises.prompt: A speaker says every conclusion, including this one, is unknowable. Which label fits?

choices.text: Skepticism
Mysticism
Reason as the means of knowledge
A call to examine one argument more carefully

feedback.note: The speaker is not offering a hidden means. The speaker is denying that knowledge is possible.

exercises.prompt: Complete how mysticism denies reason.

feedback.note: The substitute replaces reason. Mysticism’s denial is replacement, not a study of grammar or weather.

exercises.prompt: Complete how skepticism denies reason.

parts.text: Skepticism says the means of knowledge

feedback.note: Skepticism’s denial is failure: reason does not deliver knowledge. It does not crown a rival method.

exercises.prompt: Build the contrast in one line.

feedback.note: One rival keeps the aim and changes the means. The other gives up the aim.

exercises.prompt: Match each question to the stance that answers yes.

pairs.right: Yes, on the side of reason
Yes, on the side of mysticism
Yes, on the side of skepticism

feedback.note: Three yes-answers cannot all stand. This unit keeps the first and treats the other two as denials of reason.

exercises.prompt: What does this unit hold?

choices.text: Reason is the only means of knowledge; mysticism and skepticism deny that
Faith and reason are equal means of knowledge
Skepticism is the proper end of epistemology
A feeling is the standard of truth when evidence runs out

feedback.note: Reason alone is the means and the standard. Mysticism and skepticism are two ways of denying that.

exercises.prompt: Build the unit’s closing claim.

feedback.note: That claim is what mysticism and skepticism each deny, one by a rival means and one by denying knowledge.
